description: The Badass tiers: when they appear (by the PLAYER's level), how strong they are and how their guaranteed drop is shifted. Health, damage, shield, the drop floor and the names are Borderlands 2's (read from the badass survey with tools/badass_report.py, the rule: BL2 file values replace static values); the chances, speed and size are Skylands choices (BL2's own spawn rules are in its population definitions, not read). See docs/badass-roadmap.md.

columns.player_level_gate: the player's level from which this tier can appear
columns.percent: chance (percent) for an eligible enemy at the gate level
columns.per_level: percent more for every player level above the gate
columns.max_percent: the chance never goes above this
columns.max_near: at most this many of the tier alive within the pump's reach (6000 units); the badass row's number counts every tier
columns.health_mult: max health times this (a tracked temporary Health bonus)
columns.melee_damage_mult: damage of melee, bites, claws and creature attacks times this (BL2: the class's Attribute_EnemyNonWeaponDamageMultiplier against the regular class's, times the champion factor; Skyrim: AttributeDamageMult as a tracked modifier)
columns.gun_damage_mult: damage of a person's gun bullets times this (BL2: weapon damage comes from the gun; a champion only gets Enemy_Damage_PerPlayerPerPlaythroughByChampion 0.74 / 0.65 in single player; the plugin launches with LaunchData.power)
columns.rarity_shift: the drop's rarity weights move up this many rarities
columns.min_rarity: the guaranteed drop is at least this rarity (1 common ... 6 e-tech)
columns.shield_mult: LATER (better gear): the tier's shield capacity times this (BL2: Attribute_EnemyShieldMaxValueMultiplier against the regular class's); not used yet
columns.bl2_drops: how many guaranteed gun/gear items BL2 gives this tier (its loot list); Skylands gives ONE whatever the tier (the user's choice), shown for reference
columns.source: bl2+design: the columns named in bl2_columns come from Borderlands 2 (tools/badass_report.py on the badass survey), the rest are Skylands choices
columns.bl2_columns: the columns read or derived from Borderlands 2
columns.bl2_object: the Borderlands 2 object the numbers come from ('-' when none yet)

rows.bl2_columns: name_prefix health_mult melee_damage_mult gun_damage_mult shield_mult min_rarity bl2_drops
rows.note: from level 1 (the user's choice), 3 percent then +0.5 a level. BL2: health x3.0 = median over 11 regular/Badass class pairs (2.65 without the Varkid, whose regular is a larva); melee x2.28 = median non-weapon damage 2.0 x champion 1.14; one guaranteed uncommon (BadassEnemyGunsAndGear)

rows.bl2_columns: name_prefix health_mult melee_damage_mult gun_damage_mult shield_mult min_rarity bl2_drops
rows.note: bosses and dragons are at least this tier. BL2: a Super is x1.94 the health and x1.15 the damage of its family's Badass (Loader and Varkid, the only two families with a Super class; elsewhere 'Super Badass' is just the Badass's name in the second playthrough); shield x2.0 from the Loader alone; BL2 guarantees a rare + an uncommon

rows.bl2_columns: name_prefix health_mult melee_damage_mult gun_damage_mult shield_mult min_rarity bl2_drops
rows.note: a boss is Ultimate half the time from player level 25. BL2: health x5 the Badass (the Varkid, the only Ultimate class); its damage x0.75 the Badass would make it hit softer than a Super, so damage and shield are held at the Super's (a choice, to confirm); BL2 guarantees a very rare + a rare + an uncommon
